claims.text: Clinical capacity: the ability to understand the potential benefits and harms of the proposed health care and possible alternatives, and to make and communicate a health care decision.
claims.quote: Clinical capacity to make health care decisions is the ability to understand the potential benefits and harms of the proposed health care, to understand possible alternatives, and to make and communicate a health care decision.

claims.text: Who determines it: appropriate health care professionals determine clinical capacity when needed and document the determination process.
claims.quote: Appropriate health care professionals determine this type of capacity when needed and document the determination process.

claims.text: Decision-specific: clinical capacity is specific to a particular health care decision, and the level needed depends on the complexity of that decision.
claims.quote: Clinical capacity is specific to a particular health care decision and thus is limited to that decision. The level of clinical capacity needed to make a health care decision depends on the complexity of that decision.

claims.text: Can change: capacity may be intermittent, variable and affected by the environment; patients who lack capacity due to intoxication, delirium, coma, severe depression, agitation or other impairment may regain it when the impairment resolves.
claims.quote: Capacity may be intermittent, variable, and affected by the environment. Patients who lack capacity due to intoxication, delirium, coma, severe depression, agitation, or other impairment may regain capacity when their impairment resolves.

claims.text: If the patient lacks capacity: try to restore it; if that is not possible, contact the agent or proxy named in the patient’s durable power of attorney for health care or another legally authorized surrogate.
claims.quote: To obtain consent to treat a patient who lacks clinical capacity, health care professionals should try to restore their capacity. If this is not possible, health care professionals must contact an agent or proxy designated in the patient’s durable power of attorney for health care or another legally authorized surrogate

claims.text: Legal capacity (competency): a legal status that cannot be determined by health care professionals.
claims.quote: Legal capacity (also called competency) is a legal status; it cannot be determined by health care professionals.

claims.text: Presumed capable: in the United States, people aged 18 or older are presumed legally capable of making their own health care decisions.
claims.quote: In the United States, people aged 18 or older are presumptively considered legally capable of making health care decisions for themselves.

claims.text: Losing legal capacity: people remain legally capable until a judge declares them legally incapacitated, usually through a guardianship or conservatorship procedure.
claims.quote: People remain legally capable until a judge with appropriate jurisdiction declares them legally incapacitated with respect to some or all areas of functioning. This declaration usually occurs through a guardianship or conservatorship procedure in the courts.
